newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan posts year-high against US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan posts year-high against US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up slightly at a year-high of 8.3042 on Wednesday from Tuesday's 8.3043 against the U.S. dollar, on news of higher foreign exchange reserves and a rising trade surplus.
It was the third day in a row the yuan ended at a year-high on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market.
The yuan opened slightly up at 8.3040 and moved around 8.3041 for most of the session, hitting an intra-day low of 8.3046 and a high of 8.3038.
Trading was slow, with most done at 8.3041, traders said.
Dealers said that the yuan rose slightly on news of China's growing foreign trade surplus and foreign exchange reserves.
Dai Xianglong, governor of the central bank, said on Tuesday China had foreign exchange reserves of more than $93 billion.
"This news strengthened pro-yuan sentiment and made the yuan rise slowly but steadily," a dealer said.
"Selling was slow and in a range of 8.3040 and 8.3045 today," said a second dealer.
Dealers expect the yuan to rise above 8.3040 on Thursday.
The yuan closed down slightly at 7.5480 from 7.5391 against 100 Japanese yen and down at 1.0735 from 1.0732 against the Hong Kong dollar.
